verdict: Leads are being captured — tracking is broken, not demand.
narrative: In the last 28 days, your CRM recorded 46 new opportunities and Google Ads logged 12 conversions, yet the lead counter reads zero — that gap is a tracking misconfiguration, not a sign that inquiries stopped. Conversion tracking is being repaired so the numbers reflect what is actually coming in. Separately, ad spend ran erratically this period, averaging $20.82 per day over the most recent seven days against a 28-day average closer to $46 per day, which we are stabilizing. Three milestones land this Sunday — the Review Boost campaign, the financing page, and the Homer Glen branch page all go live August 31 — followed by Local Services Ads re-enabling for heating season on September 1.

watch_item.issue: Lead tracking shows zero despite real activity in both your CRM and Google Ads — the measurement, not the pipeline, is the problem.
watch_item.fix: Conversion tracking and lead form attribution are being audited and corrected now so next week's report reflects actual intake.
